expectations.text: Presents the top tier first as the anchor and makes the middle tier the visibly best value
expectations.evidence: Gold is the first column of the ladder table and is labeled '(anchor)'. The text also says 'Present Gold first as the anchor.' Silver's header carries a '(best value)' label, and the card states 'Silver is the default the card points at.' The benefits only partly back that label. Silver costs exactly half of Gold (EUR 3,000 vs 6,000) and gets exactly half the passes (3 vs 6), so it is not better value per euro than Gold. The 'best value' claim rests mostly on the label rather than on a visibly better price-to-benefit ratio, so the score is lowered from 5.

expectations.text: Presents the top tier first as the anchor and makes the middle tier the visibly best value
expectations.evidence: The top tier comes first: the Packages table opens with Headline Partner at 8,000, so it sits at the top as the anchor. The card never says it is meant as an anchor, though. Gold (5,000) gets no 'best value' or 'most popular' label, no highlight and no value comparison. Its value is not clearly better on the numbers either: Gold costs 1,250 per pass, against 1,333 for Headline, 1,500 for Silver and 1,000 for Supporter.
